correctness.rationale: In the stated conformal metric the degree-l radial multiplier F(t), t=|x|², obeys t(1-t)F''+[l+2-lt]F'+lF=0. The regular branch is 1-lt/(l+2); the other indicial exponent at zero is -(l+1). Angular orthogonality makes the radial-symbol compression scalar on each degree, of dimension (l+1)². Polar measure gives t^(l+1)(1-t)^(p-1)F(t)² dt. For l≥1, s=l(1-t) gives the stated (s+2)² tilt and upper limit min(l,a l N^(-beta)). The unnormalized densities converge in L¹ by the integrable majorant e^(-s)s^(p-1)(s+2)²; normalization then gives convergence of the cdf uniformly over all s≥0. This proves uniformity on every band l/N≥epsilon, including p<1 and the two degenerate regimes. The omitted multiplicity fraction is asymptotically at most epsilon³. Weighted Riemann sums give the critical distribution; its no-atom property also at G_p(a) gives the asserted threshold result. Integrating the small-s density gives the small-a coefficient; the exponential upper tail makes the rescaled large-a defect integral finite and positive. For p=1, with Q=1+3s/5+s²/10, the two unweighted-in-a integrals of s²e^(-s)Q and s²e^(-2s)Q² are 8 and 1121/800, giving 15837/800 after multiplication by 3. The decreasing finite radial likelihood ratio (and increasing s-tilt in the limit) gives the strict Euclidean comparison for proper tails and positive degree.

It determines threshold counts and the rate of loss of projection defect in the two ends of that transition. The explicit tilt also isolates why Euclidean weighted radial concentration is not an adequate substitute, despite the same collar scale.
